decision.rationale: Accessibility action timeout recovery now preserves dispatch evidence. Only a proven zero-write timeout is retryable; dispatched or unknown outcomes fail closed. Real subprocess counterexamples, package and root gates, release checks, and exact-head CI pass.

summary: The remediation resolves PRR-020 by retaining the worker write boundary through action transport metadata and computing one fail-closed retryability value for both protocol fields. No new blocking defect was identified, and PRR-001 through PRR-020 are resolved for the reviewed snapshot.

findings.title: A dispatched action timeout was incorrectly advertised as retryable
findings.observation: The previous warm action path suppressed internal replay but mapped every timeout to retryable protocol guidance. The current result preserves the dispatch boundary and permits retry only when requestDispatched is exactly false.
findings.trigger: A worker receives an AXPress request but its response is lost or exceeds the deadline, or the deadline expires before the worker lock can be acquired.
findings.impact: Before remediation, a consumer could retry an unknown mutating outcome and duplicate an already-executed UI action.

evidence.description: Worker results classify every pre-write result as undispatched and every write-attempted result as dispatched.
Action transport propagates known dispatch evidence and protocol mapping retries only an explicit false value.
The real pre-dispatch worker regression records zero frames and both retryability fields true.
The real post-dispatch worker regression records one AXPress, zero fallback, and both retryability fields false.
Exact-head GitHub CI passed all configured test, package, wheel, and distribution checks.

findings.remediation: Completed: preserve dispatch evidence and fail closed for dispatched or unknown mutating outcomes.
findings.verification: Completed: pre-dispatch, post-dispatch, unknown transport, non-action compatibility, resource, package, root, wheel, preflight, and exact-head CI checks pass.

required_actions.action: Preserve the action dispatch boundary, fail closed after dispatch or when unknown, and add protocol-level recovery assertions.

risks.description: Private desktop logs can contain transient UI text.
risks.mitigation: Keep raw artifacts untracked and publish bounded semantic evidence only.

risks.description: A timeout after dispatch remains an unknown desktop outcome.
risks.mitigation: Emit non-retryable recovery guidance and never replay internally.

risks.description: Contended calls can expire before dispatch.
risks.mitigation: Use one deadline, return zero-write evidence, and preserve a healthy worker.

risks.description: One worker serializes operations and can apply queue backpressure.
risks.mitigation: Bound lock waiting with the caller deadline and retain timing diagnostics.

risks.description: Action timeout recovery changes from unsafe generic retryability to dispatch-aware guidance.
risks.mitigation: Use additive transport evidence, stable status and failure kind, explicit API docs, and regression tests.

risks.description: The warm action worker remains on the direct and service path.
risks.mitigation: Revert the focused worker remediation commits if needed; no data migration exists.

risks.description: Dispatch safety spans the private worker and generic protocol mapper.
risks.mitigation: Keep the boundary explicit and retain real-subprocess contract tests.
